_comment: Batch 02 (Sets 2-3). Distractor-only rewrites; correct options and rationales unchanged.

RN-S02-01.A: A client with pneumonia who has a temperature of 101°F (38.3°C), a productive cough with yellow sputum, and SpO2 94% on room air
RN-S02-01.C: A client with COPD whose SpO2 is 90% on 2 L/min nasal cannula, which is unchanged from the client's baseline on admission
RN-S02-01.D: A client with a chest tube whose water-seal chamber shows fluctuation with respirations and 30 mL of serous drainage this shift

RN-S02-02.A: Clamp the chest tube close to the client's chest and leave it clamped until the provider arrives
RN-S02-02.C: Increase the suction to the prescribed maximum so the lung re-expands and the bubbling stops
RN-S02-02.D: Document the finding as an expected sign that the chest drainage system is functioning correctly

RN-S02-06.A: "I'll increase it right away, since more oxygen is always better for someone who is short of breath and has lung disease like your mother."
RN-S02-06.C: "Oxygen is addictive, so we try to use as little as possible to keep your mother from becoming dependent on it once she goes home from the hospital."
RN-S02-06.D: "Only the respiratory therapist is allowed to change the oxygen, so I'll ask them to come and check on your mother when they're available."

RN-S02-09.A: Using the fluticasone first, then the albuterol 5 minutes later, and rinsing the mouth after the albuterol
RN-S02-09.C: Using both inhalers back to back at the same time for a faster, stronger combined effect on the airways
RN-S02-09.D: Using the albuterol, then swallowing water afterward to prevent thrush from developing in the mouth

RN-S02-10.A: Wheezing that is louder than on arrival and now heard throughout both lung fields
RN-S02-10.C: A heart rate that increased from 104 to 118/min after the albuterol treatment
RN-S02-10.D: A productive cough with thick white sputum and wheezing on expiration only

RN-S02-15.B: A tongue depressor, a penlight, and a set of sterile cotton-tipped applicators
RN-S02-15.C: A padded tongue blade, a bite block, and a container of normal saline solution
RN-S02-15.D: A spare nasal cannula, petroleum jelly for the stoma site, and a bag of gauze pads

RN-S02-18.A: Mild soreness at the puncture site that the client rates 2 on a 0–10 scale
RN-S02-18.C: A small amount of serous drainage on the dressing, about the size of a quarter
RN-S02-18.D: The client's request to resume eating and drinking now that the procedure is over

RN-S02-19.B: Elevated central venous pressure, jugular venous distention, and peripheral edema
RN-S02-19.C: Unilateral wheezing over the right lung that clears completely with coughing
RN-S02-19.D: Hypercapnia that corrects promptly with low-flow supplemental oxygen therapy

RN-S02-24.A: Allow the client to rest without disturbing them, since the SpO2 has improved to 93%
RN-S02-24.C: Administer the scheduled nebulizer treatment and reassess the client's breathing afterward
RN-S02-24.D: Increase the oxygen to a nonrebreather mask at 15 L/min and recheck the SpO2 in 15 minutes

RN-S03-01.B: A client with multiple sclerosis who reports fatigue and leg heaviness after a morning physical therapy session
RN-S03-01.C: A client who reports a headache that worsens when sitting up 6 hours after a lumbar puncture
RN-S03-01.D: A client with Parkinson's disease whose carbidopa-levodopa is due in 30 minutes and who has a mild tremor

RN-S03-07.A: Crush the medications and mix them in applesauce so they are easier for the client to swallow
RN-S03-07.C: Give the medications with thickened liquids to reduce the client's risk of aspiration
RN-S03-07.D: Ask the client whether they have any difficulty swallowing before giving the medications

RN-S03-09.A: Turning the client onto their side to keep the airway clear
RN-S03-09.B: Loosening the clothing around the client's neck and chest
RN-S03-09.D: Noting the time the seizure began and how long it lasts

RN-S03-10.A: Administer the next scheduled dose and reassess the gait and nystagmus in 4 hours
RN-S03-10.C: Administer the next dose with food to reduce side effects such as the unsteady gait
RN-S03-10.D: Encourage the client to ambulate in the hallway with a walker to improve balance

RN-S03-11.A: Administer the prescribed PRN antihypertensive medication
RN-S03-11.C: Check the urinary catheter tubing for kinks or obstruction
RN-S03-11.D: Notify the provider of the BP and the client's symptoms

RN-S03-12.A: Bladder distention and the need for intermittent catheterization
RN-S03-12.C: Sensation and movement in the lower extremities
RN-S03-12.D: Skin integrity over the sacrum, heels, and occiput

RN-S03-13.A: Ptosis of both eyelids that worsens in the evening
RN-S03-13.B: Fatigue and leg weakness after walking to the bathroom
RN-S03-13.D: Double vision when reading or watching television

RN-S03-14.A: Deep tendon reflexes in the arms and the legs
RN-S03-14.C: Pain level and paresthesias in the legs and feet
RN-S03-14.D: Bowel sounds and the date of the last bowel movement

RN-S03-15.A: "I'll get up slowly from sitting or lying down so I don't get dizzy."
RN-S03-15.C: "My urine or sweat may turn darker, and that isn't harmful."
RN-S03-15.D: "I'll report any new jerky, twisting, or writhing movements."

RN-S03-17.A: "You're doing a wonderful job caring for your mother. Just keep going, and things will settle down."
RN-S03-17.C: "Have you considered placing her in a nursing home? That might be the best option for both of you."
RN-S03-17.D: "Most caregivers feel this way at some point. It will get easier for you as you both get used to the new nighttime routine."

RN-S03-24.A: Repeat the full neurological assessment, including pupils, in 1 hour
RN-S03-24.C: Administer the prescribed PRN analgesic for the client's worsening headache
RN-S03-24.D: Place the client flat in bed to improve blood flow to the brain

PN-S02-01.B: Auscultating the lung sounds of a resident with pneumonia and reporting any crackles
PN-S02-01.C: Adjusting the oxygen flow rate for a resident who seems short of breath during activity
PN-S02-01.D: Reinforcing teaching on metered-dose inhaler use with a resident who has asthma

PN-S02-02.A: Supine with one pillow under the head and the knees slightly bent
PN-S02-02.C: Trendelenburg, with the head lower than the feet to promote drainage
PN-S02-02.D: Left side-lying with the head of the bed flat and a pillow behind the back

PN-S02-03.A: "Breathe in through your mouth, then breathe out slowly through your nose for about the same length of time."
PN-S02-03.C: "Breathe in deeply through your nose, then hold your breath for 10 seconds after each breath."
PN-S02-03.D: "Breathe in through your nose, then breathe out forcefully and quickly through pursed lips."

PN-S02-04.A: Blowing forcefully into the mouthpiece to raise the indicator as high as possible
PN-S02-04.C: Using the device once every 4 hours while lying flat in bed with the head of the bed down
PN-S02-04.D: Taking several rapid, shallow breaths through the mouthpiece to raise the indicator quickly

PN-S02-07.A: "Collect it after breakfast, when you usually have more secretions and it's much easier to cough them up into the cup."
PN-S02-07.C: "Use mouthwash first to reduce germs in your mouth, then cough into the cup when you're ready."
PN-S02-07.D: "Spit saliva into the cup until it's about half full, then close the lid tightly and label it."

PN-S02-09.D: Mild headache on the first day of therapy

PN-S02-10.C: Gown and gloves only, without a mask
PN-S02-10.D: Eye protection only, such as goggles

PN-S02-11.D: A slow heart rate and low BP

PN-S02-13.A: Shaking the inhaler well before attaching it to the spacer
PN-S02-13.C: Breathing in slowly and deeply through the spacer after pressing the canister
PN-S02-13.D: Holding the breath for about 10 seconds before breathing out slowly

PN-S02-15.A: Eat three large meals a day and avoid snacking between meals
PN-S02-15.C: Drink large amounts of fluid with each meal to help food go down more easily
PN-S02-15.D: Eat a high-carbohydrate, low-fat diet to provide quick energy for breathing

PN-S02-16.A: Immediately after meals, while the client is still sitting up
PN-S02-16.C: Only at bedtime, once a day, to clear secretions before sleep
PN-S02-16.D: Within 15 minutes after tube feedings, when the client is most alert

PN-S02-18.A: Removing the old ties completely before placing the new ties so the area can be cleaned thoroughly
PN-S02-18.C: Tying the new ties loosely enough to fit three fingers underneath so the client is more comfortable
PN-S02-18.D: Performing the tie change right after the client eats, while the client is sitting upright and calm

PN-S02-20.A: Leave the room so the client can rest quietly without distraction
PN-S02-20.C: Tell the client firmly to stop panicking and slow down their breathing
PN-S02-20.D: Offer the client a sedative to help them calm down and relax

PN-S02-21.A: A dry, intact dressing over the puncture site with no drainage
PN-S02-21.C: The client's report of mild soreness at the puncture site
PN-S02-21.D: A respiratory rate of 18/min with even, unlabored breathing

PN-S02-22.A: Give the client small sips of water to soothe the throat after the procedure
PN-S02-22.C: Offer ice chips instead of water, since they are less likely to cause choking
PN-S02-22.D: Give the client a warm drink such as tea to soothe the throat and relieve discomfort

PN-S03-01.B: A client admitted 1 hour ago with stroke symptoms who is receiving IV alteplase and needs neuro checks every 15 minutes
PN-S03-01.C: A client with a head injury whose level of consciousness is declining and whose pupils are becoming unequal
PN-S03-01.D: A client in status epilepticus who has had continuous seizure activity for 6 minutes despite one dose of lorazepam

PN-S03-02.A: Shine the penlight directly into both eyes at the same time and compare the pupil sizes
PN-S03-02.C: Have the client look directly at the penlight while the light is moved slowly toward each eye
PN-S03-02.D: Check the pupils only if the client reports a headache or a change in vision during the shift

PN-S03-03.A: Hold the client's arms and legs firmly to prevent injury from the jerking movements
PN-S03-03.C: Place a finger or padded object in the client's mouth to keep the airway open during the seizure
PN-S03-03.D: Leave the client in the chair and go to get the RN and the emergency equipment

PN-S03-04.A: Offer the client a drink of water to help with the dry mouth
PN-S03-04.C: Ambulate the client to the bathroom to empty the bladder after the seizure
PN-S03-04.D: Ask the client detailed questions about the seizure while the memory is fresh

PN-S03-06.A: "I'll brush and floss my teeth carefully every day and see my dentist regularly."
PN-S03-06.B: "I'll keep my appointments for blood level checks even when I'm feeling fine."
PN-S03-06.D: "I'll wear a medical alert bracelet that lists my seizure disorder and medication."

PN-S03-07.A: Position the client at 45 degrees with the head tilted back slightly when swallowing
PN-S03-07.C: Use a straw for thin liquids so the client can control how much enters the mouth
PN-S03-07.D: Place food on the affected side of the mouth to strengthen the weak muscles

PN-S03-08.A: Place the call light and personal items on the client's left side so the client learns to look toward that side
PN-S03-08.C: Keep the room dark and quiet to reduce stimulation and help the client's vision recover more quickly
PN-S03-08.D: Patch the client's left eye during the day to reduce double vision and help the client focus on the right

PN-S03-11.A: "Keep your feet close together and take small, careful steps while walking."
PN-S03-11.C: "Look down at your feet while walking so you can see where you're stepping."
PN-S03-11.D: "Walk as quickly as possible and keep moving so your legs don't freeze in place."

PN-S03-15.B: "Take a hot bath in the afternoon to relax your muscles and restore your energy."
PN-S03-15.C: "Avoid all exercise, since physical activity will make your fatigue much worse."
PN-S03-15.D: "Do all your chores at once in the afternoon so you can rest for the remainder of the day."

PN-S03-17.A: Reposition the client every 4 hours while in bed and every 2 hours while seated in the wheelchair
PN-S03-17.C: Massage reddened areas over bony prominences firmly at each position change to improve blood flow
PN-S03-17.D: Keep the head of the bed at 60 degrees at all times to prevent sliding and reduce shearing on the skin

PN-S03-21.A: "Don't cry. He needs you to be strong for him right now while he recovers."
PN-S03-21.C: "He'll be back to normal after rehab. Most people recover completely from a stroke."
PN-S03-21.D: "You should ask the doctor about his prognosis, since I can't answer that for you."

PN-S03-23.A: Avoid eye drops and lubricants, since they can irritate the eye and slow the facial nerve's recovery
PN-S03-23.C: Apply warm compresses to the open eye every hour while awake to stimulate the facial muscles to close it
PN-S03-23.D: Keep the eye uncovered at night so that air can circulate and the eye can blink naturally during sleep
